one-line thesis: Lenskart delivered record revenue and margin expansion driven by deep Tier 2+ market penetration and international scaling, with AI and smart eyewear now central to its next-phase growth; the compounding effect of vertical integration and store density is unlocking unprecedented profitability and customer acquisition efficiency.
financial scorecard: revenue: +41% YoY to ₹2,516cr; EBITDA/margin: +61% YoY to ₹322cr, margin +270bps to 21.3%; PAT (rptd): ₹204cr; PAT (normalized): ₹204cr (no distortions in Q4); order book: not disclosed; net debt: net cash of ₹3,881cr (post-IPO payables settled)
guidance: revenue growth: sustained double-digit (no specific %, but compounding expected); margin: long-term steady-state EBITDA pre-Ind AS target 25%; order inflow: no specific guidance; capex/commissioning: FY27 net new stores ~FY26 level (542), plus manufacturing investments
segment / subsidiary detail: India: revenue ₹1,475cr (+44% YoY), EBITDA pre-Ind AS margin 15.3% (+600bps), 170 net new stores, 6M eye tests, SSSG 24%, Same Pincode growth 31%; International: revenue ₹1,054cr (+35.4% YoY, +25% CC), EBITDA pre-Ind AS margin 9.2% (+110bps), 13 net new stores, Japan strongest performer, Middle East resilient
growth verticals / optionality: Tier 2+ towns (183 net new stores in Q4, 542 in FY26), international expansion (718 stores globally), smart glasses (B by Lenskart, 30K+ waitlist), AI-driven automation in eye testing and manufacturing, store densification in existing pin codes
margins & cost dynamics: India product margin held flat at 64% despite rupee depreciation due to vertical integration; cost savings from automation, HQ tech efficiency, and same-store growth drove EBITDA expansion; international margins improving via ACP reduction and scale
capex / expansion: ₹603cr funded by ₹887cr operating cash flow; included 603 net new stores, Hyderabad manufacturing facility, GeoIQ tech infrastructure
capital allocation: Prioritized store expansion, manufacturing (Hyderabad, Thailand JV), AI/R&D (smart glasses, automated eye testing), and M&A (Meller); net cash balance ₹3,881cr provides flexibility for future M&A or buybacks
risks & watch-items: currency volatility (rupee depreciation), geopolitical supply chain risks (mitigated by vertical integration), competitive entry in smart glasses (Google), execution risk in AI transformation, margin pressure from mass-market campaigns
management quality / tone: Highly confident, visionary, and execution-focused; emphasized long-term compounding, AI as core strategic shift, and patient capital allocation; dismissed short-term noise, stressed customer experience and volume growth over ASP
non-obvious takeaways: 1. 45% eye test growth vs 25% unit growth implies massive conversion upside; 2. Store clustering in same pin codes is not cannibalizing but expanding demand via micro-market optimization; 3. 64% product margin maintained despite rupee depreciation signals deep structural cost control; 4. Army cantonment store in Srinagar symbolizes untapped rural/semi-urban penetration

themes.title: Quick-commerce, omnichannel & retail expansion
themes.need: Quick-commerce and value retail are the structural growth engine, and Q1FY27 rewrote the unit-economics model. ETERNAL raised Blinkit's steady-state margin from a 5-6% range to ~6% and set a first-ever 4% GAAP EBIT margin target (after ESOP and depreciation) while capex per store went from INR 1cr to INR 2.5cr (+150%) with NOV/store/day up only 60% and net working capital improving 18 to 14 days - so margin can now drift DOWN while ROCE improves. Growth also decoupled from spend: Blinkit orders +21% QoQ with MTUs above 30mn achieved on LOWER marketing spend and fewer store adds, and management called Q1 the peak of competitive intensity to date. VMM did INR 3,727cr (+18.7%) on 10% SSSG with gross margin up to 28.7% driven by lower promotional spend rather than price hikes, validated a small-format store at the same revenue/sq ft and 'pretty much the same' ROCE as large format (a ~3,000-store national opportunity), and found 20% of its quick-commerce customers had never shopped a Vishal store. SHOPERSTOP swung PAT positive (+INR 5cr vs -INR 4cr) and raised FY27 LFL guidance from 5% to ~6%; ARVINDFASN lifted gross margin 90bps to 56.7% on full-price sell-through with direct channels now 62% of sales; MEESHO cut cost per delivered order ~INR 1 QoQ despite the May fuel hike. DMART/V2RETAIL/PATELRMART on value retail; TRENT-tier branded retail via ABFRL/METROBRAND/BATAINDIA/REDTAPE.
themes.driver: Blinkit dark-store rollout at the new INR 2.5cr/store capex against the 4% GAAP EBIT target; VMM small-format expansion; festive/quick-commerce GMV. Watch ARVINDFASN's SS27 sourcing lock (next 45-60 days) - if war-inflated input costs hold, apparel pricing corrects.

hero.oneLiner: Lenskart Solutions Limited is a technology-driven eyewear company with integrated operations spanning designing, manufacturing, branding and retailing of eyewear products.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Lenskart Solutions Limited is a technology-driven eyewear company with integrated operations spanning designing, manufacturing, branding and retailing of eyewear products.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Lenskart designs and sells prescription eyeglasses, sunglasses, contact lenses and eyewear accessories under its own brands and sub-brands through an omnichannel network of websites, mobile applications and 2,806 stores globally (2,137 in India, 669 international as of June 30, 2025). It runs a centralized supply chain with in-house frame and lens design and manufacturing at Bhiwadi (Rajasthan) and Gurugram (Haryana), supplemented by facilities in Singapore and the UAE.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- Visionsure Services Private Limited — Indian Group Company: Promoter group entity with related party transactions
- Baofeng Framekart Technology Limited — Foreign Group Company / 51% Joint Venture (China): Frame manufacturing; similar line of business
- Le Petit Lunetier Paris SAS — Foreign Group Company: Similar line of business
- Owndays Inc. — Subsidiary (acquired August 2022): Japan and Southeast Asia eyewear brand
- Dealskart Online Services Private Limited — Wholly owned subsidiary (acquired December 31, 2024): India store operations
- Stellio Ventures, S.L. — Subsidiary (acquired August 2025)
- Quantduo Technologies Private Limited — Subsidiary (acquired September 2025)

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Eyeglasses:** Prescription eyeglasses, Unpowered sunglasses, Smart glasses (Phonic audio-enabled), Reading/computer glasses
- **Other eyewear:** Contact lenses (powered and unpowered)
- **Accessories:** Clip-ons, Bags, Chains, Contact lens solutions, Frame swaps, Eyedrops

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- India - retail consumers (B2C) across 28 States and 3 Union Territories, served through PAN-India retail stores plus app and website
- Japan
- Southeast Asia (Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam)
- Middle East (United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia)
- Greater China region (Taiwan, Hong Kong)
- Australia
- Europe (Spain, United Kingdom)
- Exports contribute 1.11% of total turnover of the entity

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Fully backward-integrated, centralized supply chain: in-house design of frames and lenses (since 2021), in-house frame and lens manufacturing (69.87% of prescription eyeglasses sold in FY25 made at India facilities; 6.44 million frames and 4.06 million lenses manufactured in FY25), centralized procurement of frames and lenses, lens coating/edging/cutting/polishing and assembly at Bhiwadi and Gurugram, supplemented by Singapore and UAE facilities. 75.37% of India inventory centralized at manufacturing facilities (March 31, 2025). Centralized model enables next-day delivery in 58 cities and 3-day delivery in 49 cities in India. India supply chain leveraged to serve international markets and Owndays post-acquisition.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Product margin expansion via centralized procurement and in-house manufacturing (consolidated product margin 63.88% FY23 to 67.92% FY25)
- EBITDA (excluding other income and exceptional item) margin improvement from 6.86% FY23 to 14.60% FY25 to 17.77% Q1FY26
- International segment product margin lift post-Owndays (70.42% FY23 to 74.43% FY25)
- High depreciation and amortisation and finance costs from leased store network (lease liabilities)
- Inventory centralization (75.37% centralized as of March 31, 2025)

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Increase markets' penetration and expand customer access across channels
- Strengthen manufacturing and supply chain capabilities
- Continue to innovate and expand product portfolio
- Invest in new technologies (AI, automation, cloud)
- Continue to enhance customer experience
- Continue to strengthen brand across markets

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Deepen and broaden the India store network across Metropolitan, Tier 1 and Tier 2+ cities, funding approximately 620 new CoCo stores from Net Proceeds over FY2026 to November 2028; scale international operations (Japan, Southeast Asia, Middle East) leveraging India's centralized supply chain; a non-binding MoU dated December 8, 2024 with the Government of Telangana contemplates a greenfield manufacturing facility involving investment of approximately Rupees 15,000 million.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Centralized supply chain and 75%-automated Bhiwadi manufacturing enabling scale, lower cost and next-day delivery
- In-house frame and lens engineering and manufacturing (69.87% of prescription eyeglasses sold in FY25 made in-house facilities)
- Customer-focused in-house design (105 new collections launched FY25; 109-member design team)
- Lenskart brand and portfolio of owned sub-brands spanning economy to premium (India's Most Trusted Eyewear Brand 2025, TRA)
- Technology-first approach with AI virtual try-on, computer vision and geo-analytics
- Omnichannel retail platform of 2,806 stores plus 100mn+ app downloads
- Track record of revenue growth (32.52% CAGR FY23-FY25) and margin expansion

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Raw material cost and supply concentration — Cost of raw materials consumed was 24.52% of total expenses in FY25; majority purchased on spot basis; significant frame/raw-material import dependence on China (incl. Baofeng JV).
- History of losses and negative cash flows — Restated losses in FY23 (Rupees 637.57 million) and FY24 (Rupees 101.54 million); profitability only recently achieved.
- Leased store network intensity — All retail stores and offices are leased; high lease liabilities, depreciation and finance costs; non-renewal/rent escalation risk.
- Dependence on Promoters and key personnel — Brand tied to Peyush Bansal's reputation; loss of key management could hurt operations.
- Acquisition integration — Growth relies on integrating Owndays, Dealskart, Stellio and Quantduo; synergy and goodwill impairment risk.
- Regulatory / FEMA and ED inquiry — Ongoing Enforcement Directorate inquiry under FEMA and denied ODI NOCs; pending DPIIT Press Note 3 approval.
- Competition from unorganized retail — ~77% of India prescription eyewear by value is unorganized, constraining pricing power.
- Manufacturing concentration — Almost all lens cutting/edging concentrated in the Bhiwadi-Gurugram cluster; disruption risk.

commitments.title: Promises (RHP)
commitments.body:
- **Set up approximately 620 new CoCo (Company owned and Company operated) stores in India funded from Net Proceeds over FY2026 to November 2028.**
- **Deploy Rupees 2,726.22 million of Net Proceeds towards capital expenditure for new CoCo store setup and equipment.**
- **Deploy Rupees 5,914.40 million of Net Proceeds towards lease/rent/license payments for approximately 1,118 (up to 1,530) existing CoCo stores in India.**
- **Invest up to Rupees 2,133.75 million of Net Proceeds in technology, software and cloud infrastructure.**
- **Deploy Rupees 3,200.63 million of Net Proceeds towards brand marketing and business promotion to enhance brand awareness.**
- **Proposed greenfield manufacturing facility in Telangana under a non-binding MoU with the Government of Telangana.**
- **Contractual commitment to spend Rupees 898.59 million (USD 10.50 million) on cloud infrastructure under the Cloudkeeper Agreement over three years to December 31, 2027.**

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Build a house of brands - John Jacobs, Owndays, Meller, Hooper and more to come - each serving a distinct customer and occasion, all powered by the Lenskart platform
- Own the customer journey end-to-end through a full-stack, vertically integrated system: discovery, eye test, design, manufacturing, in-store experience, delivery and lifelong care
- Use AI as an operating layer across the business, turning every customer interaction into intelligence that improves the next one
- Scale eye testing as the top of the funnel - remote optometry (168 India stores at FY25-end to 623 at FY26-end, 908 stores …
